# Results — Study 717 (Person-of-the-Year)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The question — **"does TIME's
Person-of-the-Year cover jinx the honoree's stock (a magazine-cover-curse cousin)?"** —
tested as a long-horizon **event study**: around each mid-December coronation, the
**cumulative abnormal return** (CAR over 1 / 3 / 6 / 12-month windows) is the stock's
return minus a **market-model** fit (`stock = α + β·SPY`) estimated on a clean pre-event
window, cumulated over the post-announcement window. You only learn the pick when the cover
drops, so every window starts at **+1 trading day**. Most Persons of the Year are
politicians or abstract groups with no ticker; the honoree table is the transparent census
of the **tradable** ones. Offline core + synthetic control are deterministic; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes — each honoree ticker + SPY (public, no key) |
| Honoree table | hardcoded `POY_EVENTS` (ticker, announce date, honoree, `direct`), fingerprint **ff8a712ac1d1** |
| As-of | 2026-07-12 (prices through 2026-07-10) |
| Honorees in table | **4** tradable (AMZN'99, MSFT'05, TSLA'21, DJT'24); all 4 have usable price history |
| Named-but-untradable | **META'10** (Zuckerberg — IPO 2012, not public at the cover) · **DJT'16** (Trump — no public co until the 2024 merger) |
| Benchmark / model | market model `stock = α + β·SPY`, 120-day estimation window, 5-day gap |
| Event window | CAR **[+1, +252]** trading days (canonical 12-month drift); sweep over 1m/3m/6m/12m |
| Entry / costs | short at **+1 day**; borrow **5%/yr** (a generous floor for these hard-to-borrow names) + 10-bps round-trip |

> **Two named caveats (on the Signal axis).** (1) The set is **four events** — one tradable
> business honoree per ~6 years — and the `direct`/`linked` label (honored *as* the CEO vs a
> public-company link) is the believers' framing, subjective at the margin. (2) Dropping
> META'10 and DJT'16 for lack of price history is a **survivorship** note; both were huge
> business picks. Neither moves the verdict, because the verdict turns on the *selection*
> confound (below), which is robust.

## The signal — post-coronation CAR (canonical 12-month window [+1, +252])

| honoree | ticker | 12m CAR | prior-year run-up | CAR < 0? |
|---|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| Jeff Bezos (Amazon) | AMZN | **−234.1%** | +49.9% | ✓ |
| Bill Gates (Good Samaritans) | MSFT | −11.7% | +0.8% | ✓ |
| Elon Musk (Tesla/SpaceX) | TSLA | **−146.3%** | +58.4% | ✓ |
| Donald Trump (Trump Media) | DJT | −149.8% | +106.9% | ✓ |
| **pooled** | | **−135.5%** | | **4 / 4** |

Pooled mean CAR **−135.5%**, **t = −2.95**, curse-rate **100%** (4/4 negative), placebo
**p = 0.030** one-sided-left (two-sided 0.044) against random mid-December windows on the
same names (null mean −8.1%). Taken at face value, the cover curse looks *real*: every
honoree's stock underperformed the market over the following year, and the pooled *t* clears
the desk's |t| ≥ 2 bar. The rest of the teardown is about why that face value is misleading.

## Horizon sweep — the "curse" is a slow bleed, and it's absent at one month

| window | mean CAR | *t* vs 0 | placebo *p* (left) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 month [+1,+21] | −1.5% | −0.18 | 0.477 |
| 3 months [+1,+63] | −31.4% | −3.31 | 0.062 |
| 6 months [+1,+126] | −70.3% | −3.11 | 0.024 |
| **12 months [+1,+252]** | **−135.5%** | **−2.95** | 0.027 |

There is **nothing** in the first month (t = −0.18) — no cover-day shock. The decline builds
over quarters. That timing is the first tell: a magazine *jinx* would be an announcement
event; a slow multi-quarter bleed is what **mean-reversion of an extended stock** looks
like.

## The confound — TIME crowns people at their zenith

Regress each honoree's 12-month CAR on the stock's **prior-year run-up** (the momentum going
*into* the cover):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| corr(prior run-up, post CAR) | **−0.58** |
| fit | CAR = −0.69 − 1.23 · run-up |
| **residual curse after removing run-up** | **mean −0.0%, *t* = −0.00** |

This is the whole study in one line. The honorees who fell hardest (AMZN after +50%, TSLA
after +58%, DJT after +107%) are exactly the ones who had **run up the most** before the
cover; the one crowned without a run-up (MSFT, +0.8%) barely moved. Once you subtract the
part explained by prior momentum, the "cover curse" residual is **exactly zero**. The
magazine adds nothing — TIME's editors pick zenith stocks, and zenith stocks mean-revert.

## Leave-one-out — not a single-name artifact (which makes it *worse* for the story)

| drop | pooled mean | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| — AMZN | −102.6% | −2.26 |
| — MSFT | −176.7% | −6.16 |
| — TSLA | −131.9% | −2.03 |
| — DJT | −130.7% | −2.02 |

The raw *t* survives dropping any one name (all four honorees fell), so this is **not** one
outlier. But robustness of the *raw* decline is not evidence for a *magazine* effect — it's
evidence that *all four picks were extended stocks that mean-reverted.* The confound is the
point, not the outlier.

## Tradability — costs are not the killer, capacity and path-risk are

Short each honoree at +1 day, hold 12 months, pay 5%/yr borrow + 10 bps:

| honoree | short gross | net (5% borrow + 10 bps) | worst squeeze vs the short |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| AMZN | +81.1% | +76.0% | +8.6% |
| MSFT | −13.3% | −18.4% | +14.0% |
| TSLA | +49.6% | +44.5% | **+25.2%** |
| DJT | +70.7% | +65.6% | +17.3% |
| **average** | **+47.0%** | **+41.9%** | |

Ex-post, the short *made money* (net +41.9% average). So we do **not** claim costs kill it —
they don't. It is a `MIRAGE` for three other reasons: (1) **capacity** — ~4 tradable business
honorees in 25 years is a scrapbook, not a portfolio; (2) **path-risk** — you're shorting the
most-squeezable names alive, and TSLA ran **+25%** against the short before it fell (a
margin-callable adverse excursion); (3) it's **beta, not magazine-alpha** — the residual
after prior run-up is zero, so you're running a concentrated short-momentum bet you could
hold diversified across hundreds of names instead of one cover star per presidential term.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, four events are weak

A deterministic four-event panel with meme-stock-sized noise and a **plantable**
post-coronation drift:

| planted drift | mean CAR | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **0 bps** (no curse) | −37.6% | **−1.26** |
| −3000 bps | −67.6% | −2.26 |
| −12000 bps (≈ real magnitude) | −157.6% | −5.27 |

With **no** planted edge the control's *t* is −1.26 — four extreme-vol names tilt negative by
luck but stay below 2 (no false positive). Only a large planted decline reaches significance.
The real-tape *t* of −2.95 exceeds pure four-event noise, confirming a **real decline is
present** — which the run-up regression then attributes entirely to selection. The machinery
is honest; the interpretation is the lesson.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The raw pooled 12-month decline is genuinely significant on the tape
  (**−135.5%**, *t* = **−2.95**, placebo *p* = **0.03**, 4/4 negative) — but it is absent at
  one month (*t* = −0.18), rests on **four events**, and **vanishes to *t* = −0.00 once you
  control for the honorees' prior-year run-up** (corr −0.58). Significant raw, fully explained
  by selection ⇒ WEAK, not REAL.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The realized shorts even *made money* (net +41.9% average), so
  costs aren't the killer — but four tradable honorees in 25 years is no capacity, the
  ex-ante squeeze path-risk is ruinous (TSLA +25% against you first), and the edge is
  short-momentum beta you'd never concentrate this way.
- **"Cover curse?" — MISATTRIBUTED.** The decline is real and the folklore isn't imagining
  it — but it is **zenith mean-reversion**, not a magazine jinx. TIME crowns people at their
  peak; peaks revert; the cover is a *symptom* of the extension, not its cause. Residual curse
  after prior run-up: **zero**.
